name: Hip Abduction

claims.text: Sit with the back against the pad, feet on the footrests and the pads snug against the outer thighs; set the seat so the knees line up with the machine's pivot.

quotes.text: Sit on the hip abduction machine with back against the pad, feet on footrests, and pads snug against outer thighs. Adjust seat for knees to align with pivot point.

claims.text: Hold the handles for stability and brace the core.

quotes.text: Grip handles for stability and engage core.
Adjust the machine to the appropriate settings, sit down, and grip the handles.

claims.text: Push the legs outward against the pads until they are comfortably apart (StrengthLog: as far as possible), hold briefly, then return slowly while resisting the weight.

quotes.text: Exhale and push legs outward against pads, squeezing outer hips.
Continue until legs are comfortably apart.
Hold briefly at peak contraction.
Push the pads out by moving your legs apart as far as possible.
Inhale and slowly return legs to start, resisting weight.

claims.text: Range: from knees together to a full, comfortable abduction, without overextending.

quotes.text: From knees together to full comfortable hip abduction without overextending.

claims.text: Keep the upper body still and the back flat against the pad; no momentum.

quotes.text: Keep upper body still throughout.
Back flat against pad
No momentum

claims.text: Set the machine up to fit you to avoid straining the hip, avoid weight that spoils your form, and get professional advice if the hip hurts.

quotes.text: Adjust machine for proper alignment to avoid hip strain.
Avoid excessive weight that compromises form.
Consult professional if hip pain present.

claims.text: Breathe out as the legs push out and in on the controlled return.

quotes.text: Exhale during outward push; inhale on controlled return.

claims.text: The hip abduction machine works the muscles that move the thighs apart: gluteus medius and parts of gluteus maximus; Motra also lists gluteus minimus and the TFL.

quotes.text: The hip abduction machine trains the muscles that abducts (moves apart) your thighs, like your gluteus medius and parts of gluteus maximus.
Seated machine isolation exercise targeting gluteus medius, minimus, and TFL

claims.text: Measured on a hip abductor machine (11 men): gluteus medius was more active than the TFL, and the machine had the best gluteus medius-to-TFL ratio of the three exercises tested.

quotes.text: GMed activation was greater than TFL in all exercises in both concentric and eccentric phases.
In both concentric and eccentric phases, GMed:TFL ratio was greater in HAM compared to CLAM and SLHA.

claims.text: Tempo: Motra lists 2-1-2 and its Tempo tooltip gives the order (eccentric, bottom pause, concentric, top pause): 2 s for the return, a 1 s pause at the start, knees together and 2 s for the push out. Its "Hold briefly at peak contraction." asks for a brief pause right after the push out and no source gives its seconds, so that 1 s pause is a drawing convention (LR-33).

quotes.text: Tempo 2-1-2
Hold briefly at peak contraction.
The speed for each phase of the movement, written as four numbers (e.g., 3-1-2-0): eccentric (lowering), bottom pause, concentric (lifting), top pause. Each number represents seconds.

claims.text: Load progression: add 2-10% load once you can do one or two reps more than the target number.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

claims.text: Motra names the common mistakes on the hip abduction machine: jerking the weight, arching the lower back, using the upper body to swing, an incomplete range of motion and letting the pads crash together.

quotes.text: Jerking the weight
Arching lower back
Using upper body to swing
Incomplete range of motion
Letting pads crash together

plate.viewWhy: The legs move apart in the frontal plane (c3), which reads only from the front (census: front).
plate.equipment: Seated hip abduction machine (composed, census R3): seat, back pad, footrests, two leg pads against the outer thighs pivoting at knee level, side handles (c1, c2). Floor line.
plate.start: Seated, back flat on the pad (c1, c5); knees together (c4), feet on the footrests, pads against the outer thighs (c1); hands on the handles (c2).
plate.end: Legs pushed apart to a full, comfortable range (c3, c4); upper body still, back on the pad (c5).

checkpoints.label: Knees at pivot
checkpoints.what: Seat set so the knees line up with the machine's pivot.

checkpoints.label: Full range
checkpoints.what: Legs go from knees together to comfortably wide.

checkpoints.label: Upper body still
checkpoints.what: Back flat on the pad, no rocking.

mistake.what: Incomplete range: the knees open only a little before the legs come back.
mistake.why: Motra's common-mistakes list puts "Jerking the weight" first (c12); it shows only as speed, so it cannot be drawn. "Arching lower back" shows only from the side, and "Using upper body to swing" is a swing, seen as speed. "Incomplete range of motion" is next on the list (c12), against Motra's full, comfortable range from knees together (c4), and reads from the front. No source ranks how common they are.
mistake.rankNote: No source measures how often each fault happens. LR-31 step 3: jerking the weight, first on Motra's common-mistakes list for this machine (c12; handlingMistakes[0], momentum or rocking, cites it). Step 1: no frequency word counts for a fault (Motra's "Typical Rep Range" is programming). Step 2: no named fault is tied to harm. Set aside: "Adjust machine for proper alignment to avoid hip strain." (c6) is a seat setting, not a candidate; "Do not overextend hips beyond comfort." is a Safety Note, not on the common-mistakes list or handlingMistakes, and names no harm word; "Consult professional if hip pain present." (c6) names no fault. Step 3: Motra's list, written for this machine and the anchor: "Jerking the weight", "Arching lower back", "Using upper body to swing", "Incomplete range of motion", "Letting pads crash together". Jerking shows only as speed, so drawable is false and plate.mistake names the next fault by the same steps: the arched lower back shows only from the side and the census view is front; the upper-body swing is seen as speed; the incomplete range (c12, c4) shows from the front as the knees opening only a little. Pick unchanged: plate.mistake stays the incomplete range; drawable changes from true to false because the top fault, jerking, cannot be drawn.

tells.text: Legs open wide, then fully close
Back stays flat on the pad

tempo.text: Up 2 and down 2 are Motra's 2-1-2 (c10, WEAK), whose Tempo tooltip gives the order eccentric (lowering), bottom pause, concentric (lifting), top pause (R-LB6-2); the page shows three numbers, read as the first three. Its middle 1 s is a pause at the start, knees together, between the return and the next push out, so it is named here and not written in pause (LR-33). Pause 1 is the pause right after the push out: Motra's "Hold briefly at peak contraction." gives no seconds, so the 1 s is a drawing convention (c10, WEAK; LR-33). This corrects the earlier reading that put the middle 1 s at the peak.

setup.step: Set the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot.
Sit with your back against the pad and feet on the footrests.
Set the pads snug against your outer thighs.
Hold the handles and brace your trunk.
Pick a weight you can move without losing form.

posture.point: Open from knees together to comfortably wide.

handlingMistakes.fix: Keep your upper body still. Lower the weight.
Open the legs to a full, comfortable range.

rows.where: Outer hips and side of glutes
rows.means: The hip abductors are doing the work.
Fault: a machine not set to fit you.
rows.fix: Line your knees up with the pivot.

risks.risk: A machine that doesn't fit you can strain the hip.

zooms.right: Knees level with the pivot, pads on the outer thighs.
zooms.wrong: Seat set so the knees sit far from the pivot.

libraryDiff.why: abductors primary (gluteus medius, measured, c9) and glutes primary (StrengthLog: parts of gluteus maximus; Motra lists glutes, c8) both match exercises.json. The glutes claim rests on coach sources only.
